chunks: On all this He suffers no trouble, and no impediment hampers Him in the preservation of what he created nor any languor or grief hinders Him from the enforcement of commands and management of the creatures, His knowledge penetrates through them and they are within His counting. His justice extends to all of them and His bounty encompasses them despite their falling short of what is due to Him.
ai.seo_question: How does God's knowledge and justice encompass creation despite human shortcomings?
ai.summary: In this passage from the 'Al-Ashbaah' chapter of Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) articulates the concept of Divine Omnipotence (Qudrah) and Ease (Yusr), asserting that God’s preservation of creation is free from fatigue or impediment. This reflects the Shia theological emphasis on God’s absolute self-sufficiency, where His infinite knowledge and justice encompass all beings despite their limited capacity to fully grasp His essence. The text underscores that divine bounty is not contingent upon human merit, highlighting the unmerited nature of God’s grace.
